text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT [P1] — spike in 5xxs for /v1/generate in us-west-2. error rate 18% over 10m, latency up. paging eng-oncall primary. link: https://monitoring.redwood.internal/alerts/1750001234 :rotating_light:

Anna: On it. I'm the primary for this shift. Looking at dashboards now. Miguel you're secondary — can you pick up traces if I need to escalate?

Miguel: Yep I can. Pulling trace sample. Quick ask — is this likely runtime or infra?

Anna: Initial stack traces show majority from runtime tokenizer step (OOM-ish-ish) but some 503s from loadbalancer. My hunch: runtime model lane hitting degraded nodes + LB surge.

Platform Oncall: I can check node health/ASG in us-west-2. If it's autoscaling thrash, we might be better to route traffic to us-east-1 until we mitigate.

Sam: Support Oncall here — flagging two customers in us-west-2 with traffic spikes (acme-inc, pixly). They're seeing errors in-prod. If we plan failover, need to notify them.

Jess: Quick runbook pointer: /runbooks/runtime-high-5xx (https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-high-5xx). Steps 1-3 to collect logs and trigger safe model-fallback. If we fallback, use model: small-v1-fallback to preserve latency.

Anna: Doing step 1: tails on runtime logs. Found repeated KV cache errors preceded by `std::bad_alloc` on model-worker-3/4.

Miguel: Confirmed worker restart loop on worker-3. Memory pressure high on gpu01. Could be a bad quantization change in recent model rollout.

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: model-service@2026-02-28T21:40Z by jess — rollout %: 100% — changelog: quant-opt flags enabled.

Dmitri: If deploy just changed quant flags, runtime team should be oncall for rollback. Is there a quick rollback procedure?

Anna: Yes. I can initiate a model rollback to previous image. But we should coordinate with infra before killing workers — want to avoid flapping autoscaler.

Platform Oncall: I'll pause autoscaler and drain new worker node group for us-west-2. Setting policy to fixed for the next 10m.

Security Oncall: tagging in case there's any sign of exploit — so far logs look like allocation failures, not auth anomalies. If you see suspicious requests (weird paths, mass token usage), ping me and I'll pull packet captures.

Anna: Action list so far: 1) Platform: pause autoscaler (in progress) 2) Anna: rollback model flags, trigger graceful restart of affected workers 3) Miguel: collect full traces & top-k requests 4) Support: message customers; prepare incident comms template.

Sam: Support comms draft: "We're investigating elevated errors for /v1/generate in us-west-2. We're rerouting some traffic and expect recovery within 15–30 minutes. We'll update in #status as we know more." Want me to post?

Anna: Yes post that with ETA 30m. Include workaround: clients can retry with smaller batch sizes.

Miguel: Collected traces and attaching snippet: ```
TRACE: request_id=abc123
path=/v1/generate
worker=model-worker-3
error=std::bad_alloc
mem_usage=14.9GB/16GB
```

Anna: Rolling back model-service to image model-service:2026-02-27-bak now. Running `kubectl set image deployment/model-service model=model-service:2026-02-27-bak -n prod-us-west-2`

deploy-bot: Rollout started: model-service -> model-service:2026-02-27-bak (rolling restart).

Platform Oncall: Autoscaler paused. Confirmed new nodes draining. No new worker launches for next 10m.

Anna: Restarting affected pods gracefully. Monitoring error rate...

~5m later~

Anna: Error rate down to 2.3% and falling. Latency back to baseline. Marking mitigation successful for now.

Sam: Posted update to customers and #status. Support will watch for retries/SEV tickets.

Miguel: Collected heap dumps and uploaded to /artifacts/1750001234/ for postmortem. Keeping traces for eval.

Dmitri: Follow-up items: 1) Revert quant-opt change if behavior confirmed 2) Add canary policy to prevent full rollout without metric gating 3) Add alert to detect high memory ratio per worker early.

Anna: Agreed. I'll lead post-incident writeup and schedule a blameless postmortem. Assigning action owners in the doc.

Security Oncall: No immediate security artifacts. Standby for any further suspicious indicators.

Platform Oncall: Re-enabling autoscaler, but with conservative min nodes for the next 24h.

Anna: Handoff note for next shift (Miguel taking primary at 03:00 UTC): please watch us-west-2 error-rate and autoscaling deltas, check runbook steps if it reoccurs. There's a small coverage gap from 02:45–03:00 because I'm briefly offline for handoff to happen — Miguel you cover that 15m?

Miguel: I can cover 02:45–03:15 if needed.

Sam: Support will remain on standby and will escalate any customer-facing regressions.

Anna: Thanks all. Logging incident and SLO impact. Will tag postmortem once draft is ready. :white_check_mark:
